name: Southern hawker
note: Southern hawkers (docs 11, 12, 23; M2; Matt chose the species on 2026-10-20): large green and blue dragonflies that patrol and hover over ponds and come to look at people. A few at a time, not individuals with names. LIFE. ecology: kind swarm (src/world/creatures/swarms.js keeps them in the hourly tick); dormancy names the window in recipes/world/seasons.json (late spring to autumn they fly; the rest of the year they are nymphs in the pond). needs (src/world/ecology/needs.js): five, each 0..1, mood = their weighted geometric mean. water: still fresh water depthM deep in a body of at least body.minM2 square meters (a puddle is not a pond to breed in), full within okM, none beyond maxM. Sun: they want a sunny pond; nothing shades the island yet, so it is not scored. food: the midge field over a square of radiusM, against per times the ideal group (they share the midges lightly with the frogs). shelter: perches and stems to climb out on as nymphs, each plant weighted, the best within radiusM, from 'from' and full at 'full'. quiet: low sensitivity. company: n[0] to n[2], n[1] ideal. scored: any open ground or fresh water (where: near), for the beat over the pond and its banks.
